title: The effect of additional BFR training on hand strength and hand function in rehabilitation patients with injuries of the upper extremity distal of the elbow
summary:
Blood flow restriction (BFR) training is a training method in which the targeted restriction of the blood flow in an extremity by means of a special blood pressure cuff creates a metabolic situation in which comparable muscle building effects can be achieved as with conventional training with a considerably higher training load despite a low mechanical load.
After surgical procedures, patients are often not able to tolerate high training loads. Therefore, effective muscle building is impeded or rather only possible to a limited extent. This problem may be attenuated by BFR training.
In this prospective controlled study, the effect of BFR training on the success of rehabilitation of patients with injuries of the upper extremity below the elbow is to be investigated. The aim is to find out whether additional BFR training in the context of rehabilitation has a therapeutic added value and supports the restoration of functional mobility.
The study patients are allocated by chance either into the intervention group or into the control group. In both groups, patients conduct BFR training in addition to their normal rehabilitation program for several times per week, at least ten times during their rehabilitation stay of four to six weeks. The intervention group conducts the BFR training with a cuff pressure that effectively restricts the blood flow, while the control group trains with a pressure that does not appreciably restrict the blood flow.
Primary aim of the study is the improvement of the pain free grip strength over the time of rehabilitation. Secondary aims are questionnaires on everyday function of the upper extremity (PRWE-G), on quality of life (PROMIS 29) and on pain (NRS scale). The outcome parameters are recorded at the beginning and at the end of rehabilitation stay to quantify the effect of BFR training.
conditions: Injuries to the upper extremity distal to the elbow
Distal fracture of the radius: unspecified

interventions.name: The intervention group conducts BFR training with a cuff pressure of 60-70% of the arterial occlusion pressure in addition to the standard rehab program several times per week,  at least ten times during rehabilitation stay. Outcome parameters are recorded at the beginning and at the end of rehabili

The control group conducts BFR training with a cuff pressure of ≤20% of the arterial occlusion pressure in addition to the standard rehab program several times per week,  at least ten times during rehabilitation stay. Outcome parameters are recorded at the beginning and at the end of rehabilitation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient rehabilitation due to an injury to the upper extremity distal to the elbow
Exclusion criteria:
Cadiovascular deseases:
- Coronary artery desease
- Existing or increased risk of venous thromboembolism
- Increased risk of hemorhagic stroke
- Increased risk of exercise-induced rhabdomolysis
- Increased risk of atrial fibrilation or heart failure
- Previous use of medication that is known to increase the risk of blood clotting
- Induration/Marfan syndrome
- Vascular endothelial dysfunction
- Previous hemophilia
- Cardiopulmonary diseases
- Silent myocardial ischemia
- Left ventricular dysfunction
- Iatrogenic changes in the arterial/venous vessels of the lower extremities 
- Inserted stents, bypasses
- sickle cell anemia
Other exclusion criteria: 
- Lack of knowledge of German
- Bilateral injury to the upper extremities
- Open wounds or infections of the extremities to be trained
- Amputations on the upper extremities
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Lack of German language skills
